Lee (AE): Heads-up: customer in EMEA wants an air-gapped POC. Key asks: keep transfer <5GB per patch, signed bundles, ability to rollback fast, and clarity on whether sealed POCs change pricing. Can we meet bandwidth and signing needs?
Priya (SE): We can do differential minibundles (models + config). Deltas typically compress well (snappy/lz4), but quantized model diffs can still be several GBs. Need to confirm model churn rate.
Lee (AE): They said they plan to update model weights monthly but only accept patches quarterly. Bit of a mismatch.
Priya (SE): If they only allow quarterly installs we can batch monthly changes into a quarterly minibundle. For hotfixes we can push an emergency delta (smaller) but it requires acceptance by their ops window.
Jordan (Sales Eng): Commercial: sealed/offline = Private SKU + platform fee. For POC we can issue a 90-day eval license that converts on signature. If they insist on escrowed-license or offline activation tokens, that's an add-on.
Maya (Security): Signing/attestation notes: we publish an SBOM + signature manifest. For customer re-sign flow: we provide a signing manifest + signing-tool that runs inside their HSM/KMS to produce a customer signature. Ask: do they require FIPS 140-2/3? Also confirm whether chain-of-custody docs needed for courier deliveries.
Ops (Courier): For courier: encrypted-USB in tamper-evident blister, chain-of-custody sheet, and optional notarized manifest. ETA for physical courier depends on site; budget for shipping and customs (if cross-border).
Lee (AE): What's the rollback story if a minibundle breaks a service?
Priya (SE): Keep previous full bundle on jumpbox; operator runbook: mount jumpbox -> redwoodctl restore --bundle <prev> -> restart pods. We recommend a canary node first. We'll provide a 1-page rollback checklist and a kubectl snippet.
Maya (Security): Telemetry will be off by default for sealed installs. If they want periodic usage reports we can produce an offline metrics export (CSV) that they can import. Need to confirm PII sanitization rules for logs.
Jordan (Sales Eng): SLA quirk: guaranteed patch window (e.g., quarterly within 72h) requires SOW clause + higher support tier. Also flag: discounted POC pricing ok but conversion triggers billing for reserved capacity.
artifact-bot: [artifact-sign] bundle rbundle-20241215-7a9c - size 3.9GB - sig: sig-v2.key. Verify:
```
redwoodctl verify --bundle rbundle-20241215-7a9c --pubkey redwood_pub_v2.pem
```
Priya (SE): Also checklist for customer: 1) provide acceptance window dates 2) confirm HSM/FIPS requirements 3) jumpbox specs and retention policy 4) whitelist of allowed IPs for initial sync (if any)
Lee (AE): I'll ask them to pick quarterly patch dates and confirm whether they accept emergency hotfixes.
Maya (Security): I'll draft a short security pre-read covering signing, HSM, SBOM, and audit logs.
Jordan (Sales Eng): I'll draft a POC commercial note: eval license, courier costs, SOW patch SLA options.
Lee (AE): Can we squeeze a 30m call tomorrow to align? Proposed: Wed 09:00 PT / Thu 16:00 CET.
Priya (SE): Wed 09:00 PT works for me.
Maya (Security): Thu 16:00 CET better for me (Wed I'm tied up)
